summary.intent: Debug and fix a failing email OTP login flow in the macOS desktop app (GitHub release build), then plan the versioning and release cycle strategy for all packages, apps, and crates in the monorepo.
summary.outcome: Root cause identified (split-brain API URL between Vite compile-time env and Rust runtime env), fix implemented and PR #425 created. Phase 41 added to roadmap and CONTEXT.md written capturing a full versioning strategy: PR-commit-analysis-driven release labels, `release-as` injection into Release Please config, locked API/api-client versioning, independent semver/monotonic per component, and a cascade detection action.

repo: Tauri desktop app has a split configuration problem: JS reads VITE_API_URL at Vite compile time, Rust reads it via std::env::var() at runtime — in release builds the Rust side falls back to localhost:3000
Tauri invoke rejections are plain strings, not Error objects — `err instanceof Error` is always false for Tauri errors, causing generic fallback messages to mask real errors
VITE_API_URL is set as an env var in the GitHub Actions tauri-actions step for all four platforms (web, macOS, Windows, Linux) but was not baked into the Rust binary at compile time
The project uses Release Please in manifest mode with path-based package detection; squash merges collapse per-package bump granularity into a single commit type
API, TS api-client, and Rust api-client are tightly coupled via OpenAPI spec — api-client is generated from the spec, so they should be locked to the same version
Web and desktop apps should use monotonic versioning (v1, v2); API, TEE worker, SDK packages, and Rust crates should use semver
Staging deploys are triggered by staging-v* tags; proposed new format is date-based: staging-YYYYMMDD-release-N
Docker images for API and TEE worker should use dual tags: component version (pinnable) + latest-staging (rolling)
release-please-config.json already contains the path→component mapping needed for CI label validation — no separate config needed

code.finding: Rust runtime env fallback uses std::env::var() which resolves at runtime — returns localhost:3000 in release builds where env vars are not set at launch; fixed with option_env!("VITE_API_URL") for compile-time baking
catch block used `err instanceof Error` which is false for Tauri invoke rejections (plain strings), causing 'Verification failed' to always show instead of the real error
Identical instanceof Error masking pattern exists for MFA recovery flow — fixed alongside the OTP fix
VITE_API_URL set for macOS build step
VITE_API_URL set for Windows build step — all four platform build steps confirmed to have the var set

workflow: option_env!() in Rust reads environment variables at compile time (like Vite's import.meta.env), making it safe to bake URLs into release binaries without runtime env var requirements

PR-commit-analysis approach: read all commits in a PR via GitHub API before squash merge to extract per-package conventional commit types, auto-generate release labels, then use post-merge action to write release-as into RP config — eliminates manual labeling while preserving precision
release-as in release-please-config.json forces exact version targets per package, bypassing commit-type analysis — one-shot directives consumed when RP creates the release PR
Cascade detection should happen at PR time (not post-merge) so labels are visible for review before merge
When multiple PRs contribute to the same package bump before RP's release PR merges, post-merge action must take the highest bump level (minor wins over patch)

friction: Tauri's string-based invoke rejection format is not documented prominently — the instanceof Error pattern is a natural mistake that silently masks all Tauri-side errors
The split between Vite compile-time env vars and Rust runtime env vars is architecturally invisible — no type system or config validation catches the mismatch
Release Please's path-based bump detection conflicts with the desired label-driven precision — requires the release-as injection workaround rather than a clean native solution
No native Release Please support for Cargo.toml version bumping beyond extra-files pattern — a known limitation that influenced the versioning strategy discussion
open_items: Implement PR-commit-analysis GitHub Action that reads PR commits, maps to packages via RP config paths, auto-adds release labels, and computes cascades
Implement post-merge GitHub Action that reads final PR labels and writes release-as into release-please-config.json
Implement cascade detection logic using pnpm list --json and cargo metadata for dependency graph traversal
Update staging tag format from staging-v* to staging-YYYYMMDD-release-N
Add change-detection step to deploy-staging.yml (logging only first, conditional skipping later)
Update Docker image tagging to use dual tags: component semver version + latest-staging
Configure API, TS api-client, and Rust api-client as a locked version group in RP config
Define monotonic versioning strategy for web and desktop apps in RP config
Pre-create ~70 GitHub labels for release:component:type combinations to enable autocomplete
Test locally built desktop app to confirm the OTP fix resolves the issue before the next staging release
Push new staging tag (e.g. staging-v0.34.0-rc-2 or date-based equivalent) to trigger a release build for verification after PR #425 merges
